reaction: The distinction between magma and seawater is useful.
reason: Adding metal to the magma ocean seems like a practical step toward Earth's differentiated interior.
expectation: I expect the metal to become part of the molten Earth, potentially preparing it to separate toward the core.

reaction: The droplet stage makes the separation more tangible.
reason: Gravity should draw the denser metal inward toward a core.
expectation: I expect the metal to sink and contribute to Earth's core, though the result may be an intermediate stage.

alternatives.reason: Convection may advance the crust goal, but I want to finish following the metal first.

effect: Gravity has concentrated the metal deeper inside Earth, leaving a further step toward differentiation.
reaction: The range of possible sinking pathways adds useful nuance.
reason: Combining the sinking metal with the molten Earth should advance the differentiated interior goal.
expectation: I expect a metal-rich core to form within Earth, though it may be another intermediate stage.

alternatives.reason: Convection may help with the crust, but I want to finish following the metal first.

effect: Earth now has an iron-rich core beneath a silicate mantle, completing the interior goal; the crust goal remains.
reaction: The reminder that differentiation is ongoing adds useful nuance.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and convection may advance the crust goal.

effect: Convection brings heat to the surface, where it can escape by radiation.
reaction: The connection between convection and cooling is clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination; open space should let the surface radiate heat.
expectation: I expect the surface melt to cool and perhaps begin forming crust.

effect: Surface cooling has produced crystals and a thin solid layer, bringing the crust goal closer.
reaction: The contrast between solid surface and moving hot rock below is clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should advance the formation of crustal rafts.
expectation: I expect the crystals and melt to form an early crustal layer, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The crystals formed temporary crustal rafts, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The fragile, repeatedly remade surface is a useful contrast to a permanent crust.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following metal droplets as they sank into the planet was most worthwhile: it made core formation tangible without implying that a ready-made core was inserted.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final sequence of single available combinations felt somewhat predictable, even though it clearly explained surface cooling.

surprise.text: Convection bringing hot melt to the surface helped me understand how internal heat could escape and allow crystals to form.

arbitrary.text: Combining crystals with hot melt to make crustal rafts felt less obvious than the preceding cooling step, although the result explained that crystals gathered into patches.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the physical explanations made the planet's changing interior and surface interesting, despite the predictable final choices.
